turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I've had this cough but the biggest issue is that I've been really short of breath.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, um, when did the cough start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say about 3 days ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Three days ago, OK, and uh, around that time did you also start feeling short of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, the shortness of breath has come on, I don't know within the last day or so. It's come on after that, the cough started first.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and the cough, is it a dry cough or is it a wet cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I've been bringing up some yellowish green, kind of like phlegm, so um I guess a wet cough.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so yeah, yellowish green you said.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any blood in the sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I haven't noticed any blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how much sputum are you coughing up each time? Like is it kind of the size of your fingertip or does it fill your whole palm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah, probably more like the size of like a thumb tip.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK um, and do you notice any, like pus or froth in the sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nothing like that I noticed.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and if you were to describe the sound of your cough, does it sound like it's barky or like a hacking cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I don't know, I guess hacking.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Alright, and do you hear any wheezing at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, well, maybe I guess when I'm really short of breath, yeah, wheezing, yeah.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and the shortness of breath, how severe is it? 1 to 10, 10 being the worst?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Maybe a 7?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: At seven OK, are you having issues sleeping because of your shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, well I can't tell if it's that or the cough. I mean between those two things it's been definitely interrupting my sleep.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you find there are any triggers to your coughing like like um, a particular time of the day? Triggers like you know pollen or things in your environment like pets?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No the cough has been kind of going on all day. Um, right when I get up in the morning and goes on all night, it's been getting worse to these last few days.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, um yeah, that doesn't sound great in terms of your shortness of breath. Do you find that certain positions make it worse? Or like exerting yourself makes it worse?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, not really.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you ever experienced anything like this in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any other symptoms that you have along with your coughing and sputum?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: As soon as I breath, well, I just haven't felt good like, tired, kind of weakish.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah um, along with your fatigue and feeling weak, have you experienced any dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No dizziness and I haven't fainted or anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any confusion or memory loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No concerns with my memory.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how about um, muscle aches or any sort of body aches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Alright, yeah, maybe a bit, kind of, and weak.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, alright, so let's go back to your shortness of breath. Do you have any chest pain associated with that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and do you ever feel like your heart's racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about changes to your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, those have been normal. I haven't had any diarrhea or constipation.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and no blood in your stool?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I haven't noticed any blood, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about abdominal pains?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, I don't know why, yeah, my belly's been a bit achy maybe.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about a sore throat?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, my throat felt OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good and have you experienced any loss of taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No loss of taste, but I've noticed, yeah, my smell has been kind of funny.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Your smell has been kind of funny, like you can't smell or do things smell differently than you expect them to?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, there was a candle on earlier today and I guess I couldn't really smell it, so I guess I haven't been able to smell.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok, do you have a runny nose or a blocked nose?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had to blow my nose or anything.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in your vision or hearing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, that's been normal.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any discharge or pain in your eyes or ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, that's been OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then any changes to your urine?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any pain or anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you otherwise healthy? Do you have any medical conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I have atrial fibrillation. And I do take Metoprolol for that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how long have you had A. fib?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was like 4 years ago I think it was. It was having that like, felt like my heart was racing you were asking about earlier and they did an ECG and I was told I had atrial fibrillation. So yeah, I've been on a beta blocker for three years now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, four years, and when was the last time you had an ECG?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, maybe just a couple of months ago. I think every time that I come in to see my family doctor, they they do one.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and the last time that it was done, was it normal?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, they said yeah. My heart rate's been around 80 beats per minute which is good and I haven't had any symptoms so things have been stable.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good. And then have you had any hospitalizations or surgeries in the past?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I had an inguinal hernia repair about 15 years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any complications from that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and then besides the Metoprolol, are you on any other medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Oh yeah, I take a statin and baby aspirin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and is that for the A. fib as well, the aspirin? Or is that just for other cardiovascular issues or some sort of preventative measure?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I heard it was good for people who have atrial fibrillation so I started taking it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. and let's revisit your medications at the end of today's session. I just want to make sure that you're on the medications and I just want to make sure you're on the right dose.  Does that sound good?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, certainly.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK great. And ok, so we talked about your past medical history and medications. We will talk a little bit about any allergies that you have, if you have any.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I think it's like a sulfa allergy. I received an antibiotic like that many years ago and had a rash.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK and have you had any reason to suspect that you may have taken any sulfas recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't had any antibiotics so no, really no changes.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, good and are you up to date with all your immunizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I am yeah. I've received the Zoster vaccine for shingles and also the one for pneumonia.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good, good yeah, those two we definitely recommend if you're over 65. OK, and do you know of any family history of lung conditions or heart conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think my aunt had lung cancer but she smoked her entire life.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK and how about other cancers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No other cancers.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And have you been in touch or do you think you've been in contact with any anyone sick recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Well, I visited my mother at a long term care facility just this past weekend, so I guess about just over a week ago I visited there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have there been any COVID outbreaks at the long term care?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, there has been, I thought I was like away from those areas but I have heard about outbreaks there.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK and any travel history?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No travel.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I used to smoke a pack of cigarettes a day, but I quit about, uh, about five years ago. I know four years ago it was when I found out I had atrial fibrillation. I quit.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, well that's good. Good for you for quitting. How about marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't smoke it, but I'll use some edibles I buy from the Ontario stores a couple of times per week. Just the CBD stuff.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: The CBD stuff OK. And how many milligrams?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I'm not sure, I know it's their lowest dose though.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK if it's lowest dose, it might be 2.5 milligrams.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Sounds familiar.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK good. Is there a particular reason you take these CBD edibles?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It helps me sleep.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, if it's specifically to help you sleep, we can actually try and see if there are other options for you. You know there are pills, like they are sleep aids. Or even things like melatonin that can help regulate your sleep so we can revisit other options for you if you're open to that as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK for sure. Yeah I will. Um, yeah we can talk about that later.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that sounds good and do you do any other recreational drugs?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I do not.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how about alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I don't drink anymore.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you used to drink before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yes, I just stopped a few years ago,

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and what's your living situation like right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I live in a house with my wife.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: In a house, OK. Any concerns for like old carpets, mold or asbestos in your house?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, we've renovated it over the years.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good and I apologize, but I would like to clarify three more symptoms with you. Did you say you felt like you had a fever earlier?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, maybe I've been feeling a little hot, but it's been really more the cough and shortness of breath that's been bugging me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, well we can take a temperature today just to make sure. Have you been feeling like you have night sweats or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, not really. No, I haven't noticed that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how about, um, any weight loss over the past few months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, it's been been stable.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, alright good, so that brings us to the end. Do you have any questions or concerns that you would like to clarify before we end the interview?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing today.  I was just really hoping to get, uh, whatever this is sorted out.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, you know, um, right now it looks like, it sounds like it could be an upper respiratory viral illness, so that includes COVID.  So we will do a swab for you and then send it off to the lab for PCR results. In the meantime, because you have symptoms that overlap with COVID symptoms, we do encourage isolation for 14 days. Until your symptoms are gone, sorry,  until your symptoms are gone, even if they're gone, we do suggest isolating for 14 days just to make sure you're not a carrier or could spread COVID so we do encourage that, and that includes from your husband. If possible, we will get those results in a day or two. If they are positive, we will send your results to public health who will be in touch with you to do some contact tracing to see where you may have gotten it from. If it's not COVID, it could be other viral illnesses that are going around this time of year. And if your symptoms aren't getting better on their own, and there's reason to suspect you may have a bacterial infection or bacterial pneumonia, we will follow up with you and possibly prescribe antibiotics. How does that sound?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds like a great plan.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, great so um, I will see you at the next appointment.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Thank you.
